title: Affine pushforward is perverse up to the relative dimension
statement:
Let $k$ be a field and $\Lambda$ a finite commutative ring whose additive exponent is invertible in $k$. Let $a_Y:Y	o\operatorname{Spec}k$ be a separated morphism of finite type, let $f:X	o Y$ be an affine morphism of finite type [pqf-def-affine-morphism, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], put $a_X=a_Yf$, and let $d\ge0$ be an integer such that every scheme-theoretic fibre $X_y=X	imes_Y\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(y)$, $y\in Y$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre], has topological Krull dimension at most $d$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Work in the ordinary derived categories $D(T_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$ of the small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], with the compact-support direct image $Rf_!$ of [def-amb-etale-compact-support] (compactifications exist by [thm-nagata-compactification]), the right adjoints $a_T^	imes$ of $Ra_{T!}$ [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint], $\omega_T=a_T^	imes\Lambda$ and $D_T=R\mathcal Hom_\Lambda(-,\omega_T)$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] for $T=X,Y$. Let $D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$ be the bounded constructible complexes [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes] of finite Tor amplitude. Read the support condition and the perverse classes of [def-per-support-condition, def-per-perverse-subcategories] at these finite coefficients: $\operatorname{SuppCon}(K)$ means that for every $i\in\mathbf Z$ the closed support of a sheaf (the complement of the largest Zariski open on which it vanishes; by [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative] this is the closure of the set of points with a nonzero geometric stalk) of $\mathcal H^{-i}K$ has dimension at most $i$, the empty set having dimension $-\infty$; $K\in{}^pD^{\le n}(T)$ means $\operatorname{SuppCon}(K[n])$, and $K\in{}^pD^{\ge n}(T)$ means $\operatorname{SuppCon}(D_T(K[n]))$. Then for every $n\in\mathbf Z$ and every $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$

$$K\in{}^pD^{\le n}(X)\ \Longrightarrow\ Rf_!K\in{}^pD^{\le n+d}(Y),\qquad K\in{}^pD^{\ge n}(X)\ \Longrightarrow\ Rf_!K\in{}^pD^{\ge n-d}(Y).$$

The instance used by the Fourier transform is $d=1$, for the projection $p_2:\mathbf A^1_{k_0}	imes\mathbf A^1_{k_0}	o\mathbf A^1_{k_0}$ and its base changes. These are the upstream declarations isPerverseLE_lowerShriek and isPerverseGE_lowerShriek (finite coefficients $\Lambda$, any field $k$, $K$ of finite Tor amplitude).

source.place: node lem-per-artin-gabber-affine-curve; statement read at finite coefficients as in the upstream Lean WeilConjectures.SixFunctors.Etale.Perverse.Operations

proof.text: Three formal facts are used throughout. (a) $Rf_!$ is an exact functor of triangulated categories, in particular it commutes with shifts [def-amb-etale-compact-support], and $D_T(M[m])\cong D_T(M)[-m]$ because $R\mathcal Hom_\Lambda(-,\omega_T)$ is exact and contravariant in its first variable [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. (b) If $\operatorname{SuppCon}(M)$ and $e\ge0$ then $\operatorname{SuppCon}(M[e])$: $\mathcal H^{-i}(M[e])=\mathcal H^{-(i-e)}(M)$ has closed support of dimension at most $i-e\le i$. (c) $\operatorname{SuppCon}$ is closed under extensions: for a distinguished triangle $M'\to M\to M''\to M'[1]$ the sequence $\mathcal H^{-i}M'\to\mathcal H^{-i}M\to\mathcal H^{-i}M''$ is exact, so $\mathcal H^{-i}M$ vanishes on every Zariski open on which both outer sheaves vanish, and its closed support lies in the union of the two outer ones, whose dimension is the maximum of theirs.

source.place: 1.3 and 2.1.2: shifts and extension closure of the support condition

proof.text: Support side. Let $K\in{}^pD^{\le n}(X)\cap D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$ and put $K'=K[n]$, so $\operatorname{SuppCon}(K')$ holds and $K'$ is bounded with constructible cohomology sheaves $F_i=\mathcal H^{-i}K'$ [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes]. The closed support of $F_i$ has dimension at most $i$; in particular $F_i=0$ for $i<0$. By (a) the claim $Rf_!K\in{}^pD^{\le n+d}(Y)$ is $\operatorname{SuppCon}((Rf_!K')[d])$. The truncation triangles of the standard t-structure on $D(X_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$ [lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles] build $K'$ from the finitely many objects $F_i[i]$ by extensions. Since $Rf_!$ is exact, (c) reduces the claim to $\operatorname{SuppCon}((Rf_!F_i)[i+d])$ for each $i\ge0$. Now $\mathcal H^{-m}((Rf_!F_i)[i+d])=R^{q}f_!F_i$ with $q=i+d-m$, and [lem-per-finite-compact-support-fibre-support-bound], applied with $a=i$, bounds the dimension of its closed support by $i+d-q=m$. This is the support condition.

source.place: 4.2.4 and the fibre dimension count behind 4.1.1; fibres of an affine morphism of relative dimension d

proof.text: Exchange. For every $M\in D(X_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$ there is a natural isomorphism $D_YRf_!M\cong Rf_*D_XM$. Indeed the composition isomorphism $Ra_{Y!}Rf_!\cong Ra_{X!}$ [lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons] gives, by uniqueness of right adjoints, $f^\times a_Y^\times\cong a_X^\times$, hence $\omega_X\cong f^\times\omega_Y$. The internal adjunction [prop-asd-internal-adjunction], applied with $K=\omega_Y$, is $Rf_*R\mathcal Hom_\Lambda(M,f^\times\omega_Y)\cong R\mathcal Hom_\Lambda(Rf_!M,\omega_Y)$. All schemes are of finite type over $k$, hence Noetherian, and $f$, $a_Y$, $a_X$ are compactifiable by [thm-nagata-compactification]. No finiteness theorem and no biduality is used here.

source.place: 4.1.2 (duality exchanges Rf_! and Rf_*); the ordinary etale form of the exchange D_Y Rf_! = Rf_* D_X

proof.text: Cosupport side. Let $K\in{}^pD^{\ge n}(X)\cap D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$ and put $L=D_X(K[n])$, so $\operatorname{SuppCon}(L)$ holds by definition. By [lem-per-finite-coefficient-dual-constructible], applied to the bounded constructible complex $K[n]$, $L$ lies in $D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$ and has constructible cohomology sheaves. Since $f$ is affine, [lem-per-finite-affine-direct-image-support-bound] gives $\operatorname{SuppCon}(Rf_*L)$. By the exchange of Step 3 and (a), $D_Y((Rf_!K)[n-d])\cong D_Y(Rf_!(K[n]))[d]\cong(Rf_*L)[d]$, which satisfies the support condition by (b), as $d\ge0$. Hence $Rf_!K\in{}^pD^{\ge n-d}(Y)$. The argument gives the stronger affine bound $Rf_!K\in{}^pD^{\ge n}(Y)$ (the case $d=0$ of (b)).

source.place: Theorem 4.1.1 (Artin's affine estimate for Rf_*) and Corollary 4.1.2

proof.text: Both implications hold for every $n$, which is the statement. If $X$ is empty, $Rf_!K=0$ lies in every class. For $p_2:\mathbf A^1_{k_0}\times\mathbf A^1_{k_0}\to\mathbf A^1_{k_0}$ the morphism is affine of finite type and each fibre is $\mathbf A^1_{\kappa(y)}$, of dimension one, so $d=1$; the same holds after any base change $Y'\to\mathbf A^1_{k_0}$ with $Y'$ separated of finite type over $k_0$.
